title: 3D Printing Architecture
subtitle: Architecture prototype study pairing a printed spatial model with process animation
overview: 3D Printing Architecture presents a model-based design study where fabrication logic, townhouse scale, surface continuity and physical prototyping sit at the center of the work. The exhibit focuses on the object and its process animation: a compact way to read geometry, making and spatial intention together.
storyHtml:
This project treats 3D printing as more than a presentation output. The printed model becomes a design instrument: it tests how surfaces meet, how interior and exterior logic can be read through one object, and how fabrication constraints shape architectural decisions.

The model carries the atmosphere of a compact residential prototype. Openings, massing, thickness and layered edges are legible through the object itself, while the process video gives the work a time-based reading that still images cannot provide.

In Focus mode, the exhibit intentionally stays simple: a rotatable model and one animation page. That pairing keeps attention on the artifact and the making process without turning the project into a full documentation archive before the surrounding SPACE room is complete.

The current entry should be read as an architecture and fabrication study. It records an interest in physical modeling, material translation and the feedback loop between digital geometry and a made object.
